business_name: Adelaide Partitions and Ceilings Pty Ltd
contact_role: Patricia oversees administration, accounts, payroll, compliance and project support. Patrick holds BLD186942 and runs site supervision and OHS.
can_pay_20k: HIGH - "more than 90 commercial packages above $250,000 - totalling over $100 million in combined project value" since 2006
pain_acuteness: VERY HIGH - one named human IS the system. Patricia personally runs administration, accounts, payroll, compliance and project support for a business turning over $100M of packages. That is a job description a $20k app replaces most of.
bespoke_justification: MEDIUM-HIGH - wall and ceiling packages price by m2 and linear metre, then run measure -> install -> variation against a builder's programme. Your tiler app already does takeoff, scheduling, site records and variations - this is the same shape in a different trade.
reachability: EXCELLENT - two named directors, four named staff total, no procurement layer, no gatekeeper. Patricia is the buyer and the user.
why_not_just_buy_servicem8: They could. Your wedge is not features, it is that Patricia's whole role is bespoke to how APC runs, and a generic app makes her change her process rather than the reverse. Also: bigpond.com email in 2026 means zero prior software investment to defend.
the_opening_line: Ask Patricia what her Monday morning looks like. She runs accounts, payroll, compliance and project support for 90+ commercial packages. Do not open with software - open with her workload.
risk: Family business, so price sensitivity is real and personal. $20k needs to be framed against the cost of a part-time admin hire, not against a SaaS subscription.

contact_role: Named on the company LinkedIn page; role not stated
can_pay_20k: HIGH - "over 35 vehicles on the road", $20m public liability and $10m professional indemnity cover, LinkedIn band 11-50 employees, founded 2002
pain_acuteness: VERY HIGH - the single most quotable line in the whole dataset: "We have an emergency afterhour service company who divert calls to oncall technicians to ensure afterhour calls are acted upon promptly." They are PAYING AN ANSWERING SERVICE to do dispatch.
bespoke_justification: VERY HIGH - fire protection runs on AS 1851 servicing schedules, per-device test records and asset registers per building. Generic trade apps handle jobs, not assets with statutory test intervals. This is a genuine build, not a config.
reachability: GOOD - Paul Ware named on the company page, landline published, 8 employees discoverable on LinkedIn. No email published anywhere on the site.
why_not_just_buy_servicem8: ServiceM8 has no concept of a fire asset with a statutory next-test date. Neither does Tradify. Simpro does, at enterprise pricing and a long implementation. That gap is exactly $20k wide.
the_opening_line: They outsource after-hours dispatch to a call-answering company. Ask what it costs them per year, and what happens when a diverted call reaches the wrong technician at 2am.
risk: No email published, so it is a phone-first approach. Paul Ware's role is unconfirmed - he may not be the decision maker.

contact_role: Named on the company LinkedIn page; surname matches the company, so almost certainly owner - CONFIRM
can_pay_20k: MEDIUM-HIGH - delivers packages on FMC Redevelopment, New Mount Barker Hospital and Modbury Hospital Health Precinct. Health projects at that scale pay well. Family owned.
pain_acuteness: HIGH - "Every doorset checked, installed and functioned against the hardware schedule, with item-level ITP records supporting every sign-off." Someone is maintaining item-level inspection records by hand across five major hospital sites.
bespoke_justification: HIGHEST IN THE DATASET - item-level ITP (Inspection & Test Plan) records against a hardware schedule is not a feature any off-the-shelf trade app has. Nor is FF&E tracking or fire-door compliance. This can only be built.
reachability: GOOD - landline, info@ inbox, Damien Kolen named on the company page. Small enough that the owner takes the call.
why_not_just_buy_servicem8: There is no off-the-shelf product that produces a doorset-level ITP pack for a hospital handover. None. This is the cleanest bespoke case on the list.
the_opening_line: Ask how long it takes to assemble the ITP handover pack at the end of an FMC-sized job, and who does it. That is the demo.
risk: SIZE UNVERIFIED AND POSSIBLY SMALL - only 5 employees are discoverable on LinkedIn. That is discoverable profiles, not headcount, but qualify size on the first call before investing time.

why_not_just_buy_servicem8: Honestly, they might. Rank this one for the REFERRAL, not the build.

Win Master Linings and you are introduced to the entire AWCI membership in Australia. Price accordingly - this one is worth doing at cost.

can_pay_20k: MEDIUM-HIGH - 25+ years trading, $25m public liability cover, specialist plant fleet (material hoists, conveyor belts, void covers)
pain_acuteness: HIGH - "we test and certify every scaffold we build to meet or exceed the requirements of NZ/AS 1576" and "will issue JSA and WSMS when required". Per-scaffold certification plus per-job safety docs, produced manually.
bespoke_justification: HIGH - scaffold is stock-allocation plus erect date plus dismantle date plus hire period plus handover certificate per structure. Generic job software models none of that well. Scaffolders are chronically underserved.
reachability: MEDIUM - mobile number only. No email address published anywhere on the site.
why_not_just_buy_servicem8: ServiceM8 cannot tell you which 40 metres of your stock is on which site and when it comes back. That is the scaffolder's actual problem and nobody sells it off the shelf.
the_opening_line: Ask how fast they could produce the AS 1576 certificate for a scaffold they erected eight months ago if a regulator asked today.
risk: Phone-only contact. Also check Hillsley Scaffolding (three depots, info@hscaff.com) as the same pitch to a larger operator.

contact_role: Directors and owners - they personally bought the business in 2006 and still run it
can_pay_20k: MEDIUM - 26 years of ABN history, dedicated premises, commercial air conditioning sector specialist
pain_acuteness: MEDIUM-HIGH - a single admin@ inbox and one landline is the entire published intake for a 30-year-old commercial contractor
bespoke_justification: MEDIUM - commercial HVAC has service history per plant item and maintenance schedules, which generic apps handle poorly, but this is a softer case than fire or scaffold
reachability: BEST ON THE LIST - two named owner-directors who bought the business themselves. One conversation, one decision, no committee.
why_not_just_buy_servicem8: Weaker case here. Lead with 30 years of job history that nobody can search, rather than with compliance.
the_opening_line: Mike and Mark bought this business in 2006. Ask them where the last 20 years of job records live and what happens when a client asks about a unit they serviced in 2019.
